claims.claim_vi: Effective Go: concurrency is structuring a program as independently executing components; parallelism is executing calculations in parallel for efficiency on multiple CPUs; Go is a concurrent language, not a parallel one.
claims.verified_by: Read from the pinned commit; the sentence is in the document.

claims.claim_vi: asyncio is a library to write concurrent code with async/await and is often a perfect fit for IO-bound, high-level structured network code.

In CPython, because of the GIL, only one thread executes Python code at once; use multiprocessing or ProcessPoolExecutor to use multi-core machines; threading remains appropriate for several I/O-bound tasks; free-threaded builds of Python 3.13 can disable the GIL.

Measured by the author on 2026-10-19 (Python 3.13.16, 4 cores): four 0.5 s waits take 2.00 s one by one and 0.50 s with asyncio or four threads; four CPU-bound loops take about 0.6 s one by one, about 0.7 s with four threads and 0.21 to 0.30 s with four processes (two runs).
claims.verified_by: Run by the author; the code is described in the lesson's deep-dive section. Numbers depend on the machine.
